title: Reflective Studs & Motorway Markings
whatItIs: Reflective studs light up in your headlights and show where the lanes and edges are, even at night or in fog.
keyFacts: Driving on the left: red studs are on your left, amber studs on your right.
Green studs mark the edge of the main carriageway at slip roads and lay-bys.
Green and yellow studs show temporary layouts, such as roadworks.
A solid white edge line marks the left edge of the carriageway, next to the hard shoulder.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT enter chevrons bordered by a solid white line, except in an emergency.

items.title: Red
items.text: The left edge of the carriageway, next to the hard shoulder.

items.title: Amber
items.text: The right edge, next to the central reservation.

items.title: White
items.text: Between the lanes (or the middle of an ordinary road).

items.title: Green
items.text: Where a slip road or lay-by joins or leaves.

items.title: Green and yellow
items.text: Temporary layouts, such as roadworks and contraflows.

items.title: Chevrons
items.text: Hatched areas edged with a solid line: you MUST NOT enter unless it's an emergency.

onTheTest.question: On a motorway, what colour are the studs between the left-hand lane and the hard shoulder?
onTheTest.why: Red studs mark the left edge of the carriageway. Amber studs mark the right edge, by the central reservation.

traps: Amber is on the right, by the central reservation, not the left.
Green studs don't mean "go": they mark slip roads and lay-bys.
Green and yellow studs are temporary: expect roadworks.
